title: Ōkami
shortDescription: Hideki Kamiya and Clover Studio's sumi-e watercolor masterpiece, casting players as sun goddess Amaterasu in the form of a white wolf.
historicalSignificance: A monumental high-art achievement in video games, praised for its breathtaking traditional Japanese woodblock print aesthetic and the innovative 'Celestial Brush' mechanic allowing players to paint directly onto the screen.

editorialContent.overview: Taking inspiration from classic Shinto mythology, players inhabit Amaterasu, the Japanese sun goddess reincarnated as a majestic white wolf accompanied by the pint-sized artist Issun, journeying across Nippon to purge the land of the eight-headed demon Orochi.
editorialContent.gameplay: Open-ended exploration in the vein of The Legend of Zelda, revolving around the 'Celestial Brush': pausing the action turns the screen into rice paper, allowing players to paint calligraphy strokes to cut barriers, summon cherry blossoms, redirect water, and draw bombs.
editorialContent.technicalInnovation: Pushed the PlayStation 2 to its graphic limits with custom cel-shading algorithms that rendered live ink-bleed effects, rice paper textures, and blooming flora in real-time.
editorialContent.culturalImpact: Won widespread critical acclaim and Game of the Year awards, hailed as the finest non-Nintendo Zelda-style adventure game ever created and a pinnacle of interactive fine art.
editorialContent.preservationNotes: Preserved on PS2 DVD-ROM, ported to Wii with motion controls, and remastered in 4K HD across all modern consoles.

verifiedFactualData.sales: Over 4 million copies sold across original and HD remasters
awards: IGN Overall Game of the Year 2006

technicalSpecs.soundChip: 5-disc traditional Japanese folk orchestral score by MONACA
